title: Canonical lisse coefficient-Hom comparison is invertible
statement: Let l, E, m≤n, A, B and φ be as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-sf-etale-finite-coefficient-hom-arrow]. Let S be a scheme and K,N objects of the unbounded derived category of A-modules on S_et [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with K dualizable and etale locally isomorphic to A^r[0] (r≥0) [def-sf-finite-free-hom-evaluation-coordinates], and N bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in [c,d], c≤d [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Then the canonical comparison RHom_A(K,N)⊗^L_A B→RHom_B(K⊗^L_A B,N⊗^L_A B) is an isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraphs 2–3, lisse degree-zero specialization of the site-perfect stratum argument

proof.text: Let U be a member of the trivializing covering. The pullback of N to U is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in [c,d], so it has a bounded flat model P [lem-sf-flat-model]. By [lem-coef-etale-finite-free-hom-local-identity] the source and target coordinates are invertible and the local comparison followed by the target coordinates equals the source coordinates; hence the local comparison is invertible.

source.place: Paragraphs 2–3, lisse degree-zero specialization of the site-perfect stratum argument

proof.text: By [lem-coef-etale-perfect-hom-restriction] for the dualizable K, the pullback of the global comparison, followed by invertible Hom restriction maps and the scalar pullback isomorphism, equals the local comparison; so the pullback of the global comparison to every member of the covering is invertible.

source.place: Paragraphs 2–3, lisse degree-zero specialization of the site-perfect stratum argument

proof.text: Geometric stalks are conservative and every geometric point lifts to the covering [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]; hence the global comparison is an isomorphism. The existential comparison arrows equal the canonical ones by the heterogeneous equalities of the two lemmas, the types being definitionally equal.
